task.title: Regression: slugify keeps separator runs and edge hyphens
task.statement: Regression report for slugkit.slugify(text). Since the last change the function returns 'hello--world' for 'Hello--World', 'a---b' for 'a -- b' and 'end-' for 'end!'. The intended behaviour, which the existing tests only partly cover, is: lower-case the text; every maximal run of one or more characters that are not ASCII letters a-z or ASCII digits 0-9 becomes exactly one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are removed; an input with no ASCII letters or digits (including the empty string and whitespace-only text) returns ''. Non-ASCII letters such as 'é' are separators, not kept characters (so 'café crème' is 'caf-cr-me'). Keep raising TypeError for non-string input, keep returning a str, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing without modifying them. Fix the regression in slugkit/core.py.
acceptance_criteria: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', slugify('(parens)') == 'parens' (no leading or trailing hyphen).
slugify('') == '', slugify('!!!') == '', slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).

Existing behaviour is preserved: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug', slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3', slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'.
Non-ASCII letters are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' and slugify('日本語') == ''.
The result is a str; TypeError for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'] and b'bytes'.

interface_contract.name: slugify
interface_contract.behavior: Convert text to lowercase. Replace each maximal contiguous sequence of characters that are not in the set [a-z0-9] with a single hyphen ('-'). Remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the result. If the resulting string is empty (i.e., the input contained no ASCII letters or digits), return an empty string. Non-ASCII letters (e.g., accented characters, non-Latin scripts) are considered separators and are replaced by hyphens (and collapsed). The function returns a string.
error_cases: Raise TypeError if text is not a string (e.g., None, int, float, list, bytes).

acceptance_criteria: slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).
slugify('日本語') == '' (non-ASCII letters are separators, no ASCII alnum yields empty string).
The result is always a str.
TypeError is raised for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'], b'bytes'.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing tests' bodies changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant, with every result structurally sound and bound to its nonce); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception, whatever its origin, is never overridden (only a test the supervisor killed at its timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

A mutant counts as killed only when a sealed test failed with an authentic child result under a structurally sound supervisor run; lost, forged, incomplete, non-isolated, crashed or timed-out runs are unknown and excluded from the mutation score, and `attest check` recomputes the classification from the raw results.
